scenes.title: IN
scenes.narration: IN checks whether a value matches any item in a supplied list, replacing long OR chains.

scenes.title: Matching a set
bullets: Tests membership in a list of values
Can accept a subquery as the list
scenes.narration: IN tests whether a column's value appears in a set of listed options. It reads far more cleanly than stringing many OR conditions together. The list can even be produced by a subquery, making IN flexible for dynamic sets.

scenes.title: Matching several values
scenes.narration: This query keeps employees whose department is any of the three listed values. IN checks membership against that small set in one concise expression. The result gathers staff from all three departments together.

scenes.heading: IN vs OR chain
scenes.narration: IN expresses set membership in a single tidy clause that is easy to extend. Writing the same logic with OR forces you to repeat the column name for every value. As the list grows, the OR version becomes noticeably harder to read.

scenes.text: Use IN to test membership in a set, keeping multi-value filters short and readable.
scenes.narration: Reach for IN whenever you would otherwise chain several OR conditions on the same column, since it stays concise and clear.
